Melbourne: Albert Park and the city skyline
Albert Park is built on public roads around the lake, open to traffic for most of the year.
Shanghai: The track layout is shaped like 上 (shang), the first character of Shanghai.
Suzuka: Suzuka is F1's only figure-of-eight - the track crosses over itself on a bridge.
Miami: The circuit wraps around Hard Rock Stadium, home of the Miami Dolphins.
Montréal: The circuit is on Île Notre-Dame, an island built for Expo 67.
Monaco: The Monaco Grand Prix was first held in 1929.
Barcelona: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya opened in 1991.
Spielberg: The Red Bull Ring started life as the Österreichring in 1969.
Silverstone: Silverstone hosted the first ever F1 World Championship race, on 13 May 1950.
Spa-Francorchamps: At just over 7km, Spa is the longest circuit on the calendar.
Budapest: In 1986 the Hungarian GP became the first F1 race behind the Iron Curtain.
Zandvoort: The circuit sits in the dunes and has two steeply banked corners.
Monza: Monza opened in 1922 and is known as the Temple of Speed.
Madrid: 2026 is the first year of the Madring, a new circuit around the IFEMA trade-fair grounds.
Baku: The track squeezes past the Old City walls through a gap only about 7.6m wide.
Kuala Lumpur: Sepang hosted the Malaysian GP from 1999 to 2017 - this year it hosts the Bahrain GP.
Singapore: Singapore hosted F1's first night race, in 2008.
Austin: COTA's first corner climbs a hill about 40m high.
Mexico City: At about 2,200m it is the highest circuit on the calendar, and the track runs through a stadium.
São Paulo: Interlagos runs anticlockwise - it was Ayrton Senna's home race.
Las Vegas: The Welcome to Las Vegas sign
The race runs late on a Saturday night, straight down the Strip.
Lusail: Lusail was built for MotoGP in 2004; F1 first raced there in 2021.
Abu Dhabi: The Yas Marina hotel straddles the track, and the race runs from day into night.
